sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface staining (anti-GFP, non-permeabilized, 4°C) detected only the N-terminal ECFP fusion, confirming the N-terminus is extracellular and the tag is surface-accessible. The C-terminal EYFP fusion was detected only after permeabilization, confirming the C-terminus is intracellular. GFP-TMEM10 showed plasma membrane localization and process accumulation. No myelin-formation or other functional assay was reported for the tagged constructs.
sites.rationale: The topology has no signal peptide (raw topology begins with O at residue 1), so the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus and the only surface-accessible junction. L5 definitively establishes this by showing that ECFP-Tmem10 (N-terminal fusion) is detected by anti-GFP antibody on non-permeabilized living cells, while Tmem10-EYFP (C-terminal fusion) is not, placing the N-terminal junction unambiguously on the extracellular face. L7/L8 corroborate with GFP-TMEM10 plasma membrane signal. insert_after_residue=0 (prepend) is the only valid extracellular junction; residue_after is M (residue 1, verified from sequence). PMC2396630 generated ECFP-Tmem10 (N-terminal ECFP fusion) and Tmem10-EYFP (C-terminal EYFP fusion) of full-length human Tmem10 (OPALIN) expressed in Oli-neu cells; live-cell anti-GFP surface staining at 4°C was used to determine membrane orientation. PMC6400977 independently expressed GFP-TMEM10 in Oli-neu cells and detected GFP signal on the plasma membrane and along leading edges of extending processes.

sources.claim: We found that only the N-terminal ECFP-fusion protein was detectable by surface staining, whereas premeabilization of the cells uncovered both fusion proteins (Fig. 3B ).

literature_notes: L6 (pcDNA3.1myc, C-terminal Myc) and L9-L11 (OPALIN-HA) both place tags at the C-terminus (residue 141), which is intracellular per L5; these are recorded in other_positions. L9-L11 use the naming convention 'OPALIN-HA' (suffix = C-terminal), and the 'surface display' language in L9 refers to the protein being membrane-localised, not that the HA epitope is extracellularly accessible — consistent with the intracellular C-terminus established by L5. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion: the extracellular domain (residues 1–35) is a single uninterrupted stretch with no loop sub-structure, and no paper reports a tag inserted within it at a specific internal residue. The N-terminal prepend is therefore the only qualifying surface site.

literature_other_positions.note: pcDNA3.1myc places a Myc tag at the C-terminus (residue 141 E); L5 shows the C-terminus is intracellular (Tmem10-EYFP detected only after permeabilization).

OPALIN-HA (C-terminal HA by naming convention) expressed in HEK293T cells; 'surface display' refers to membrane localisation of the protein, not extracellular accessibility of the HA tag, which is at the intracellular C-terminus.
